title: Your hardware. Your agents.
voice: OwnBot runs open weight AI agents on your own computer. Connect tools, carry out tasks, and review changes from a dashboard on another device.
caption: Run agents on hardware you control.

title: Why local is useful
voice: Small open weight models and efficient runtimes make more tasks practical on everyday hardware. Local inference can keep model inputs on your machine and avoid per request inference fees. Speed and quality still depend on the model and hardware. Connected tools may still contact external services.
caption: More control. Hardware and model choice still matter.

title: Set up once in the terminal
voice: Configure the model and tools in the terminal. OwnBot checks structured output and tool calling before allowing agent loops. This is a capability check, not a promise that the model will always be right.
caption: Configure in the CLI. Control tasks from the dashboard.

title: A sandbox, not a real AI model
voice: For this demonstration, a tiny scripted model runs inside a disposable test computer. It does not think or run model weights. The OwnBot daemon, permission checks, dashboard, and audit trail are real.
caption: SIMULATED MODEL · real daemon and policy checks

title: A write waits for your decision
voice: Here the test agent requests a note. OwnBot pauses before calling the writing tool. Review the exact request in the dashboard, then approve and resume. The sandbox verifies zero writes before approval and exactly one afterward.
caption: Review the request. Approve explicitly. Then execute.

title: Control it from another device
voice: Use a private network connection or an SSH tunnel to reach the dashboard from another device. Cellular access is not supported yet. The sandbox proves the tested workflow. Real models, real accounts, and physical devices still need their own checks.
caption: Your computer runs it. You decide what changes.
